title: Global Consortium Launches Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library (QOBLIB) to Track Path to Quantum Advantage - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM Quantum, Zuse Institute Berlin, TU Berlin and Purdue have launched QOBLIB, an open-source, model-independent benchmarking library of 1,264 instances across ten NP-hard optimization classes, published in Nature Computational Science, to referee quantum-vs-classical advantage claims. Notably, classical solver progress since the preprint nearly doubled the largest solved Market Split instance from 60 to 110 variables, raising the bar quantum hardware must clear.

insights.claim: An international consortium led by IBM Quantum, Zuse Institute Berlin, Technische Universitat Berlin and Purdue University has published the Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library (QOBLIB) in Nature Computational Science, creating a standardized, model-independent framework for comparing quantum, classical and hybrid optimization algorithms across ten NP-hard combinatorial problem classes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A peer-reviewed, vendor-neutral benchmark makes quantum advantage claims falsifiable — expect it to become the reference marketing and procurement teams are held to.
insights.quote: the open-source initiative establishes a standardized, model-independent benchmarking framework to evaluate quantum, classical, and hybrid algorithms across ten NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem classes
insights.locator: An international research consortium led by IBM Quantum

insights.claim: QOBLIB curates 1,264 problem instances (the "Intractable Decathlon") spanning ten classes — Market Split, LABS, Minimum Birkhoff Decomposition, Steiner Tree Packing, Sports Tournament Scheduling, Portfolio Optimization, Maximum Independent Set, Network Design, Capacitated Vehicle Routing and Topology Design — with sizes from 2 variables up to roughly 3 million.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The instance-size range shows where near-term quantum hardware can even compete: the compact QUBO-mappable classes (MIS at 17–4,000 variables, LABS at 2–100) are the realistic near-term battlegrounds, not the million-variable problems.

insights.claim: The stated rationale for QOBLIB is that heuristic quantum optimization methods such as QAOA and quantum annealing lack theoretical performance guarantees, so any empirical advantage claim must be validated against state-of-the-art classical solvers rather than asserted.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Discount vendor advantage claims for annealing/QAOA that are not benchmarked head-to-head against modern classical MIP solvers.
insights.quote: while heuristic algorithms like the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) or quantum annealing lack theoretical performance guarantees, empirical advantage claims require rigorous comparisons against state-of-the-art classical solvers
insights.locator: QOBLIB addresses a critical gap in quantum optimization

insights.claim: QOBLIB is deliberately model-independent — instances can be formulated as MIP, ILP, MIQP or QUBO depending on the execution platform — and is paired with a public web portal hosting a live registry of best-known classical and quantum solutions plus an automated submission builder that validates pull requests for reproducibility.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A live public leaderboard turns quantum advantage into a continuously monitorable metric — a cheap, high-frequency signal for tracking which vendors are actually gaining ground.

insights.claim: Classical solver advances since QOBLIB's initial preprint nearly doubled the largest solved Market Split instances from 60 to 110 variables, mechanically raising the threshold quantum processors must beat to claim practical advantage.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The classical target moves faster than most quantum roadmaps assume — a structural headwind for the commercialization timelines quantum optimization vendors are marketing.
insights.quote: solver advancements since QOBLIB’s initial preprint release have nearly doubled the largest solved Market Split instances from 60 to 110 variables, elevating the performance target required for quantum processors to claim practical advantage
insights.locator: Broad Ecosystem Adoption and Baseline Dynamics

insights.claim: At launch QOBLIB logged over 2,600 benchmark submissions from 24 contributing institutions, spanning industrial end-users (E.ON Digital Technology), national supercomputing centers (STFC Hartree Centre, Forschungszentrum Jülich), universities (National University of Singapore, USC, City University of Hong Kong) and commercial quantum software vendors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Participation by a utility end-user and two national HPC centers signals that quantum optimization evaluation has moved from pure academia into buyer-side due diligence.
insights.locator: At launch, the library logged over 2,600 submissions

insights.claim: The commercial quantum software firms submitting to QOBLIB at launch — Q-CTRL, Kipu Quantum, Aqarios, Qunova Computing, ParityQC, JIJ and Qoro Quantum — constitute a visible competitive shortlist of the quantum optimization software layer willing to be benchmarked publicly.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch which of these names climb the live leaderboard — and note which large hardware vendors are absent from the submission list.
insights.locator: commercial quantum software providers (Q-CTRL, Kipu Quantum
